name: Monastery of Geghard and the Upper Azat Valley
description: Geghard is a medieval monastery in Armenia's Kotayk province, tucked against the sheer cliffs of the Azat River gorge. Many of its churches and chambers are carved straight into the mountain, some reaching deep inside the rock, and the grounds are scattered with intricately engraved khachkars (cross-stones). Its name means "spear," recalling the relic said to have been kept here, though the site began in the 4th century around a sacred spring in a cave.
